I have no aquarium experience and have recently started looking into starting one. I'm fascinated by anemones but have no idea what I would be getting into trying to keep one. Anyone have experience, advice, discouragement?

From what I've gathered so far, I need a large reef tank that is properly matured (I've read up to 12 months?), very high quality water conditions, and a powerful full spectrum light.
How feasible is keeping an anemone?

A reef tank is rather difficult to handle for a beginner and I would highly recommend against it. However, if you are intent on continuing with a salt reef tank first, then there are a few things to know.

-Usually the minimum size of a reef tank is 29 gallons. More experienced people can go smaller but the upkeep has to be constant. -Good lighting is a must. A reef tank can get many different diseases if the lighting isn't sufficient. -Circulation is a must. If the water is too stagnant, then several different coral and anemone species cannot thrive. -The larger the tank the more stable the water quality. The more water, the harder it is for any outside contaminates to change the PH or water chemistry.

These would be the more general things I know. I typically go for tropical and planted tanks, so you can take this with a grain of salt.
I would not recommend starting with a reef but with experience anemones are totally able to keep.
Would not recommend, as well. BUT, you can always look into starting out with a nano reef, or even starting something small in freshwater to get a feel for it :)
Reef tanks are very picky about water quality but as @longlostbleu says try a nano to start with. You will make mistakes and learn from them if you persevere with it.
